Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:11:1.hebrew: והוא שעסוקין כו' - הא דקאמר רבי יוסי דיו, והוא שהיו עסוקים בדיבור עיסקי קידושיהן עד שעת נתינה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:11:1.english: And provided that they were engaged, etc. - That which Rabbi Yosei says, “It is sufficient for him” — [this is] provided that they were engaged in speaking about the matters of their betrothal until the time of the giving.

Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:13:1.hebrew: מנא ידעה - כיון דבשעת נתינה לא עוסקין בדיבור הקידושין, מנא ידעה שלשם קידושין הוא נותנם לה שתתרצה? ואע"פ שדברו כבר בכך, הרי פסקו אותו עסק:
Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:13:1.english: From where does she know - Since at the time of giving they are not engaged in speaking of betrothal, from where does she know that he is giving them to her for the sake of betrothal, so that she will consent? And even though they already spoke about this, behold, they have ceased that discussion.

Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:13:2.hebrew: מענין לענין - שפסקו מלדבר בקידושין ממש, והיו מדברים בדברים אחרים. ומיהו, לדבר צרכי זיווגם היה, כמו: כמה יש לך נדוניא, וכמה שדות יש לך להתפרנס מהם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:13:2.english: From topic to topic - That they stopped speaking about actual betrothal and were speaking of other matters. However, it was to discuss the needs of their marriage, such as: "How much dowry do you have?" and "How many fields do you have to make a living from?"

Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:14:1.english: In the nature of bills of divorce - In their laws.

Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:14:2.hebrew: לא יהא לו עסק עמהן - להיות דיין בדבר, שמא יתיר איסור ערוה, וזהו עיוות שאינו יכול לתקן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:14:2.english: He should have no dealings with them - To serve as a judge in the matter, lest he permit a forbidden relation, and this is a distortion that cannot be repaired.

Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:14:3.hebrew: אפי' לא שמיע ליה - הא דהלכה כרבי יוסי, נימא נמי דלא יהא לו עסק עמהם? כלומר, מי שכיחא הא, או לא שכיחא, שיהא אדם נותן גט או קידושין לאשה ואינו מפרש:
Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:14:3.english: Even [if] he did not hear it - [Regarding] this [ruling] that the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, shall we also say that he should have no dealings with them? That is: Is this [case] common, or is it not common, that a person would give a bill of divorce or betrothal to a woman and not specify?

Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:15:1.hebrew: וכן בגירושין - כמו: ״אמר מר: וכן בגירושין כו'״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:15:1.english: And similarly, with regard to divorce - [This is] as if [it said]: “The Master said [above]: ‘And similarly, with regard to divorce,’ etc.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:15:2.english: It is obvious - [This is read] in a calm tone [i.e., as a statement, not as a question].

Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:1:1.hebrew: לישני בתראי - דקאמר בהו אין כאן בית מיחוש, בין דקידושין, בין דגירושין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:1:1.english: The latter expressions - [Those] about which he said, 'There is no room for concern here,' whether of betrothal or of divorce.

Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:2:1.english: Let it teach them together - Why do I need [it] to teach 'she is betrothed,' 'she is betrothed' twice?

Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:3:1.english: United - An expression of: “And they shall become one flesh” (Genesis 2:24).

Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:3:2.hebrew: מיועדת - לשון אשר לא יעדה (שמות כא), שהוא לשון קידושין באמה העבריה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:3:2.english: Designated - An expression of: “Who did not designate her” (Exodus 21), which is an expression of betrothal with regard to a Hebrew maidservant.

Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:3:3.english: My helper, my counterpart - An expression of: “I will make him a helper corresponding to him” (Genesis 2:18).

Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:3:4.english: My closed one - An expression of: “And He closed up the flesh” (ibid.).

Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:3:5.hebrew: עצורתי - לשון עצרת, שתהא נאספת עמי לבית. ורבותי אמרו: לשון ״כי אשה עצורה לנו״ (שמואל א כ״א:ו׳). ולא נהירא, דההיא ״עצורה ממנו״ קאמר, דהא אחימלך אמר לו לדוד: ״אם נשמרו הנערים אך מאשה״, ודוד אהדר ליה: ״אשה עצורה לנו״, והננו טהורים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:3:5.english: My gathered one - [This is] an expression of gathering [atzeret], [meaning] that she will be gathered with me into the house. And my teachers said: [It is] an expression [in the sense of], “For woman has been withheld for us” (I Samuel 21:6). And [this] does not seem correct, for that [verse] means “withheld from us”; for behold, Ahimelech said to David: “If the young men have kept themselves from woman,” and David replied to him: “Woman has been withheld from us” — and we are pure.

Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:6:1.english: And [is] Judea “and furthermore” to a verse - And does the verse need support from the custom in Judea?

Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:6:2.hebrew: שכן ביהודה כו' - אבל מקרא ליכא למילף, דההוא יחוד בעלמא הוא, שהרי בשפחה כנענית הכתוב מדבר, שאין קידושין תופסין בה. ומעיקרא הוה סלקא דעתיה כמ"ד בגיטין (דף מג.), בחציה שפחה וחציה בת חורין הכתוב מדבר, דשייכי בה צד קידושין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:6:2.english: As in Judea, etc. - But from the verse it cannot be derived [that she is betrothed], for that is mere designation, since the verse speaks of a Canaanite maidservant, upon whom betrothal does not take effect. And initially, [the Gemara] thought in accordance with the one who says in Gittin (43a) that the verse speaks of [a woman who is] half-maidservant and half-freewoman, in whose case an aspect of betrothal applies.

Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:7:1.hebrew: במאי עסקינן - בהנך לישני דקא מיבעיא לן אי הוו קידושין או לא, ה"ד? אי בשאין מדבר עמה קודם לכן על עיסקי קידושין, וכן בהנך לישני דגירושין, שלא היה מדבר עמה על עסק גיטה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:7:1.english: With what are we dealing - Regarding these formulations about which we were inquiring whether they effect betrothal or not, what is the case? If [we say it is] where he was not speaking with her beforehand about matters of betrothal — and likewise regarding those formulations of divorce, that he was not speaking with her about the matter of her bill of divorce.

Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:7:2.hebrew: מנא ידעה כו' - כלומר, אפילו הוו הנך לישני לשון קידושין, היכי מקדשא? הא לא ידעה מאי קאמר לה, שתתרצה להתקדש לו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:7:2.english: From where does she know, etc. - That is to say, even if these expressions were language of betrothal, how could she become betrothed? Behold, she does not know what he is saying to her, so that she would consent to be betrothed to him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:7:3.hebrew: ואלא במדבר - מה לי אי לא הוה לשון קידושין? אפילו לא אמר לה מידי נמי, אלא שנתן לה — קי"ל דהוו קידושין כר' יוסי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:7:3.english: Rather, where he was speaking - What does it matter to me if it was not an expression of betrothal? Even if he did not say anything to her at all, but only gave [it] to her, we hold that it is a [valid] betrothal, in accordance with Rabbi Yose.

Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:7:4.english: Her bill of divorce and her betrothal - Either her bill of divorce or her betrothal.

Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:9:1.hebrew: ה"נ - דמקדשא כרבי יוסי, דאמרינן: מסתמא לשם קידושין נתן, והיא קבלתם לכך. אבל השתא דפריש הנך לישני, אם לשון קידושין הן — נתקדשה, ואם לשון לבוא לעשות מלאכתו הם — הרי גילה בדעתו שאינו חפץ לקדשה עכשיו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 6a:9:1.english: So too - That she is betrothed in accordance with Rabbi Yose, for we say: Presumably he gave [the money] for the sake of betrothal, and she accepted it for that [purpose]. But now that he specified these expressions, if they are expressions of betrothal, she is betrothed; and if they are expressions of coming to perform his work, he has revealed his intention that he does not desire to betroth her now.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 6a:14:1.hebrew: לא יהא לו עסק עמהן - פי' בקונטרס: לא יהא דיין בדבר, שמא יתיר איסור ערוה, וזהו עיוות שאינו יכול לתקן. והר"ר עזריאל פי' שלא ידבר עם הנשים על עסקי קידושין לקדשם, שפעמים שתהא מקודשת באמירתם או בנתינתם ולא יבין. וקשה: תינח בקידושין; בגירושין — מה בכך אם יסבור שאינה [מגורשת]? ושמא איכא למיחש לכהן. מיהו, לישנא דעמהן לא משמע הכי, דאין אדם יכול ליתן גט אלא לאשתו. ועוד, דלקמן בפרקין (קידושין דף יג.) משמע שיש חשש איסור אשת איש, דאמר: "וקשין לעולם מדור המבול". ומיהו, יש לומר דאיכא למיחש אם פשטה ידה וקבלה קידושין מאחר:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 6a:14:1.english: "He should have no dealings with them" - The Kunteres [Rashi] explained: He should not serve as a judge in the matter, lest he permit a forbidden union [ervah], and this is "a crooked thing that cannot be made straight" [Ecclesiastes 1:15]. And Rabbi Azriel explained that he should not speak with women about matters of betrothal to betroth them, for sometimes she may become betrothed through their words or through their giving, and he will not realize [it]. And this is difficult: This is understandable regarding betrothal; [but] regarding divorce, what of it if he thinks that she is not [divorced]? And perhaps there is reason to be concerned [that she might subsequently marry] a kohen. However, the phrasing "with them" [in the plural] does not imply this, for a man can give a bill of divorce only to his [own] wife. And furthermore, later in our chapter (13a), it implies that there is a concern regarding the prohibition of a married woman [eshet ish], as [the Gemara] says: "And they are harder on the world than the generation of the Flood." However, one can say that there is reason to be concerned if she stretched out her hand and accepted betrothal from another.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 6a:14:2.hebrew: אפי' לא שמיע ליה - פירוש: אדם שנתמנה אגיטין וקידושין, צריכין אנו להודיעו הא דרב יהודה אמר שמואל שלא יכשל בה, דשכיחא; או דילמא ליכא למיחש להכי, דלא שכיחא כולי האי? וכן משמע מתוך פירוש הקונטרס:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 6a:14:2.english: "Even if he did not hear it" - Explanation: [Regarding] a person who was appointed over [matters of] bills of divorce and betrothals, must we inform him of this [ruling] that Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said, so that he does not stumble in it, as it is common; or perhaps there is no need to be concerned about this, as it is not so common? And so it is implied by the commentary of the Kuntres [Rashi].

Tosafot on Kiddushin 6a:3:1.hebrew: עצורתי מהו - פי' בקונטרס: לשון עצרת, שתהא נאספת עמי בבית. ורבותי מפרשים: לשון "כי אשה עצורה לנו", ולא נהירא, דההוא "עצורה ממנו" קאמר, דהא אחימלך אמר לו לדוד: "אם נשמרו הנערים אך מאשה", ודוד אהדר ליה: "אשה עצורה לנו, והננו טהורים", עכ"ל. ור"י מיישב לישנא דקרא כפירוש רבותיו, דה"פ: כי אשה שהיתה אצלנו — מתמול שלשום היה זה, אבל עכשיו אנחנו טהורים. וניחא, דכל אלו הלשונות השתא לישנא דקרא:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 6a:3:1.english: "[If he said: You are hereby] my gathered one, what is [the halakha]?" - [Rashi] explained in the Kuntres: "[This is] an expression of gathering [atzeret], that she should be gathered with me in the house. And my teachers explain [it as] an expression of 'for a woman has been detained with us' (I Samuel 21:6). But it is not clear [to me], for that [verse] means [that a woman was] withheld from us, as Ahimelech said to David: 'If the young men have kept themselves only from women' (ibid. 21:5), and David replied to him: 'A woman has been withheld from us, and behold we are pure' (see ibid. 21:6)." — Until here are his words. And the Ri resolves the wording of the verse in accordance with the explanation of his [Rashi's] teachers, for this is its explanation: For [even] if a woman was with us — that was yesterday and the day before, but now we are pure. And this works out well, as all of these expressions are now biblical expressions.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 6a:6:1.hebrew: משום שנא' והיא שפחה נחרפת לאיש - וסבר דקרא מיירי בחציה שפחה וחציה בת חורין המאורסת לע"ע, וכמ"ד בהשולח (גיטין דף מג.) דקידושין תופסין בה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 6a:6:1.english: Because it is stated: “And she is a maidservant espoused to a man” - And [the Gemara] maintains that the verse is dealing with a half-maidservant half-free woman who is betrothed to a Hebrew slave, and [this is] in accordance with the one who says in [chapter] HaSholeiach (Gittin 43a) that betrothal takes effect for her.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 6a:6:2.hebrew: שכן ביהודה קורין לארוסה חרופה - ודוקא ביהודה, אבל בעלמא לא; דקסבר דבשפחה כנענית הכתוב מדבר, שאין קידושין תופסין בה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 6a:6:2.english: "As in Judea they call a betrothed woman a ḥarufa" - And [calling a betrothed woman a ḥarufa is] specifically in Judea, but elsewhere not, for [the Gemara] maintains that the verse is speaking of a Canaanite maidservant, on whom betrothal does not take effect.
